headline: Fact vs Myth Discussion Activity for ESL Content-Area Classes
outcomes: Students evaluate the truth of claims using critical reasoning, not just guessing or test-taking heuristics
Encounter and discuss target vocabulary embedded in plausible factual claims
Build listening comprehension by processing and responding to information-dense statements
Develop the language of probability and hedging — 'this is likely true because,' 'I doubt this because'
howItWorks: The AI presents a series of claims about your topic — a mix of genuine facts and convincingly wrong myths
Students discuss each claim and vote true or false on their device with a brief written justification
The truth is revealed with a full explanation — highlighting key vocabulary from the lesson
The teacher uses each reveal as a teaching moment, connecting back to lesson content
teacherUseCases: Content-based language teaching where lesson facts are embedded in a detection activity
Pre-reading activity to activate prior knowledge and surface misconceptions before a text
Vocabulary in context — students encounter key terms in realistic sentences before formal teaching

faq.q: How does this differ from Two Truths and a Fabrication?
faq.a: Fact Detective presents claims one at a time for true/false evaluation, with detailed explanations. Two Truths presents three simultaneous statements for comparative judgment. Both build critical thinking but through different discussion structures.

faq.q: Are the myths completely invented or based on real misconceptions?
faq.a: The AI generates myths that reflect common misconceptions or plausible-sounding false beliefs — not random nonsense. This makes the reveal more educational and the discussion richer.

faq.q: Can I review the claims before class?
faq.a: Yes. Teachers can preview all claims and explanations before starting the session and remove any that don't fit the lesson focus.

faq.q: What do students need to participate?
faq.a: Each student votes and justifies their choice on their phone or tablet in the browser. No download or student account required — the teacher's session link is all they need.

faq.q: What language level suits Fact Detective best?
faq.a: Fact Detective works from A2 upward. At lower levels, use short, concrete claims with simple vocabulary. At higher levels, the claims can feature complex structures and academic vocabulary.

faq.q: Is Fact Detective free to use?
faq.a: Fact Detective is free. Students join the session through a browser link — no app installs or student accounts needed.
